attributes.body_ja:
「はもちろん」は、(A) は明（あき）らかにそうだと認（みと）めた上（うえ）で、(B) についても考（かんが）えるべき・言（い）うべきだと言（い）いたいときに使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）です。この表現（ひょうげん）では、副助詞（ふくじょし）の「は」が、(A) が話題（わだい）であることを表（あらわ）して、副詞（ふくし）の「もちろん」が、(A) が当然（とうぜん）であることを示（しめ）します。そのあと、文（ぶん）の (B) の部分（ぶぶん）で、話（はな）し手（て）が「言（い）うべきだ」と思（おも）っている内容（ないよう）が続（つづ）きます。また、「はもちろん」は漢字（かんじ）で「は勿論（もちろん）」と書（か）かれることもあります。

「はもちろん」は、名詞（めいし） (A) のあとに置（お）かれて、そのあとに名詞（めいし） (B) が続（つづ）きます。この文法（ぶんぽう）は、「(A) だけでなく (B) も」や「(A) は当然（とうぜん）、(B) も」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

この表現（ひょうげん）は、基本的（きほんてき）に (A) が当（あ）たり前（まえ）と言（い）いながら、(B) も (A) と同（おな）じだと言（い）うときに使（つか）われます。そのため、名詞（めいし） (B) のあとには「も」が付（つ）くことがほとんどです。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「はもちろん」は「だけでなく」と同（おな）じような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われますが、「はもちろん」の方（ほう）が、よりフォーマルな表現（ひょうげん）です。普段（ふだん）の会話（かいわ）で使（つか）うこともできますが、かたく聞（き）こえることがあります。
attributes.body:
はもちろん, or occasionally は勿論（もちろん）, is a phrase in Japanese that presents (A) as being something obvious, while (B) should still be considered/mentioned. In this expression, the adverbial particle は presents (A) as being a stand-alone topic, before the adverb もちろん 'naturally' emphasizes that (A) is what it is. After this, the (B) part of the sentence will describe some other factor that is worth mentioning.

はもちろん will be used directly after noun (A), before the sentence will go on to discuss noun (B). This construction can be translated as 'not only (A), but (B)', 'not to mention (A), (B)', and other similar English expressions.

In many cases, despite (A) being the obvious factor, (B) is being highlighted as sharing similar qualities to (A). This means that in はもちろん sentences, も will almost always be seen after (B).

Caution

While quite similar in meaning to だけでなく, はもちろん is quite a bit more formal. Due to this, it may sound quite stiff in friendly conversation, unless particularly emphasizing something.

attributes.body: だけでなく and はもちろん both express non-exclusivity, but differ in nuance and emphasis. だけでなく simply means 'not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 英語だけでなく、日本語も話せる ('He can speak not only English, but also Japanese.'). In contrast, はもちろん implies the first thing is obvious, while the second is more notable, e.g. 英語はもちろん、日本語も話せる ('He can speak English of course, but also Japanese.').

second_relatable.title: はもちろん
second_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

attributes.body: はもちろん and はもとより both mean 'not only... but also'. はもちろん adds the nuance of 'of course (A), and also (B)', e.g. 学校はもちろん家でも勉強する ('He studies at home, not just at school'). はもとより is more formal and emphasizes that (A) goes without saying, e.g. 親はもとより先生も反対した ('Not only his parents but also his teacher opposed it').

attributes.body: はもちろん emphasizes the obviousness of the first item before adding another, e.g. 英語はもちろん中国語も話せる ('He speaks not only English but also Chinese'). に加えて simply adds one thing to another without that emphasis, e.g. 雨に加えて風も強い ('In addition to the rain, the wind is also strong').

attributes.body: はもちろん highlights an obvious example together with a more unexpected addition, e.g. 寿司はもちろん納豆も食べる ('He eats not only sushi, but also natto'). をはじめ is used to give a leading example from a larger group, e.g. 校長先生をはじめ多くの人が来た ('Many people came, starting with the principal').

first_relatable.title: はもちろん
first_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

attributes.body: はもちろん highlights an obvious example together with a more unexpected addition, e.g. 子供はもちろん大人も楽しめる ('Not only kids, but adults too can enjoy it'). ばかりでなく is more neutral, simply listing two things, e.g. 雨ばかりでなく雪も降った ('It not only rained, but also snowed').

first_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

second_relatable.meaning: Not only…but also, As well as

attributes.body: はもちろん emphasizes something obvious before adding another case, e.g. 日本人はもちろん留学生も来た ('Not only Japanese people but also exchange students came'). に限らず expands the scope of a statement, implying 'not limited to (A), also (B)', e.g. 子供に限らず大人も楽しめる ('Not only children, but also adults can enjoy it').

first_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

second_relatable.title: に限らず
second_relatable.meaning: Not just, Not only… but also

attributes.body: Both express 'not only (A), but also (B)', but the nuance differs. はもちろん stresses (A) as obvious, e.g. 寿司はもちろん納豆も食べる ('He eats not only sushi, but also natto'). だけでなく gives equal weight to both, e.g. 映画だけでなくドラマも好きだ ('I like not only movies, but also TV dramas').
